name: Barak (son of Abinoam)
title: Israel's war general under Deborah
summary: Barak was a military leader from Kedesh in Naphtali who led Israel's forces to victory over the army of Jabin, king of Canaan, commanded by Sisera. He acted in faith on the words of the prophetess Deborah, even though he insisted that she accompany him into battle. He is mentioned in Hebrews as an example of faith.

keyEvents.title: The Call from Deborah
keyEvents.description: The prophetess Deborah called Barak and delivered the Lord's command to gather ten thousand men from Naphtali and Zebulun to fight against Sisera.

keyEvents.title: Barak's condition
keyEvents.description: Barak refused to go to war unless Deborah accompanied him, which led to the prophecy that the honor of victory would fall to a woman.

keyEvents.title: Gathering of the Army
keyEvents.description: Barak gathered ten thousand men at the foot of Mount Tabor, as Deborah had commanded.

keyEvents.title: Victory over Sisera
keyEvents.description: With the Lord's help, Barak led the army to a overwhelming victory by the Kishon River, where Sisera's chariots and his entire army were defeated.

keyEvents.title: The Song of Deborah and Barak
keyEvents.description: After the victory, Deborah and Barak sang a song of praise together that honored the Lord for deliverance and described the battle in poetic form.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned as an Example of Faith
keyEvents.description: In Hebrews, Barak is mentioned among the heroes of faith who by faith accomplished great things for God.
